heading: Runtime errors (-200..-299)
text:
## Runtime errors (-200..-299) [NERR.6]

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DS_ERR_FACT_INVALID`     | `ds_engine_retract` was handed a fact handle that holds no fact. Every handle the engine hands out holds one, so a caller obeying [NFCT.3.2] does not meet this code. A handle whose fact is not live, or one another engine handed out, is not this code: passing one is undefined behaviour, and no status reports it ([IDAT.1.6]) |
| `DS_ERR_ACTION_FAILED`    | a callback's own report that it failed: the call that fired the callback returns it ([NCBK.1.5]). libds raises it for no condition of its own, and a `call` with no call callback is `DS_ERR_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` instead ([NERR.7]) |
| `DS_ERR_TIME_RANGE` (-205) | a `Time` outside the representable nanosecond range (≈1678–2262), or a `Date` outside the same range — a hard error, not a silent integer wrap (LTIM.1.1.5, LTIM.1.2.2) |
| `DS_ERR_NAN_REJECTED` (-216) | a NaN `Float` rejected at `ds_engine_assert`, or as a call argument, which refuses the call ([LEXP.4.2]) — NaN must not enter working memory or a payload; `Inf` is allowed. Increments `ds.facts.nan_rejected_total` |
| `DS_ERR_JSON_NONFINITE` (-217) | a host call that would put a non-finite `Float` (`±Inf`, or a NaN) into a `Json` value, such as `ds_json_new_float`, is refused with it and changes nothing; it holds no engine, so no metric moves ([LGRA.5.8.10]). A rule's path does not return this code. There a non-finite `Float` forced into a JSON data-plane body, the `cache` value or a `Json` call argument, is a `NOT_REPRESENTABLE` trap at the verb ([LDET.3.2.7]): the activation is abandoned there, the verb does not run, so no invalid `inf` token reaches the wire, and `ds.json.nonfinite_total{verb}` increments. The trap's `ComputationError` on the stream is its report ([NCBK.2.8]) |
| `DS_ERR_SERIES_NO_BACKING` (-218) | a series aggregation read that no *declared* backing can answer — the emit plan asked for a value nothing computes — or a read whose backing query failed. The rule still has to match on something, so it receives the aggregation's cold value (`LSER.19.8`) and the error is stashed, surfacing from `ds_engine_pump` rather than being returned from the read. Distinct from "no samples yet", which stays silent and is expected: backend instances allocate lazily (`LSER.9.1.1`) |
| `DS_ERR_SCHEMA_HASH_MISMATCH` (-219) | `ds_engine_assert_external` met a `FactExternal` whose `schema_hash` differs from the program's schema of that name — a record from a changed schema, read before migration ([NCBK.10.4]) |
| `DS_ERR_FACT_REF_CONFLICT` (-220) | `ds_engine_assert_external` met a nested fact reference whose key a different live fact already holds; nothing was asserted ([NCBK.10.4]) |
| `DS_ERR_JSON_LIMIT` (-221) | a `Json` value the host hands the engine — a slot value, JSON text to parse, a call response, a cache entry — would exceed one of its limits: depth, node count, string bytes, or text length ([LGRA.5.8.6]). The call is refused and changes nothing; nothing is truncated. The status is the whole refusal: no event is recorded |
| `DS_ERR_ENCODING` (-222) | text the host hands the engine is not well-formed UTF-8: a `String` slot value at `ds_engine_assert`, JSON text at `ds_json_parse`, a string or key at `ds_json_new_string` or `ds_json_object_set`, a seed at `ds_engine_cache_seed`, or a call's response ([LSTR.8.5]). The call is refused and changes nothing; nothing is repaired. The status is the whole refusal: no event is recorded |

-201 and -203 are reserved and never reused ([IERR.2.5]).
